strategies.summary: Determine the daily directional bias from how daily fair value gaps behave inside weekly PD-array context. A same-direction daily FVG that is touched and then respected sets the bias for the following days, while filled counter-trend daily FVGs strengthen the opposite draw on liquidity.

timeframes.notes: Read daily fair value gaps inside weekly PD-array context. The 1d and 1w candles are Binance UTC-aligned, not New York-midnight candles; the entry model is separate from this bias framework.

custom_signals.name: htf_pd_array_tap
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price trades into a higher-timeframe discount array (bullish) or premium array (bearish), such as a fair value gap or order block.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: (low <= bullish_fvg[0].gap_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_fvg[0].gap_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled@bias_tf) OR (low <= bullish_ob[0].zone_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_ob[0].zone_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated@bias_tf)

custom_signals.name: fvg_touched
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price trades into the fair value gap (a touch or sting), without requiring the consequent encroachment.

custom_signals.name: fvg_respected
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price wicks into the fair value gap without a candle body closing through it.

custom_signals.name: htf_opposing_pd_array
custom_signals.plain_definition: The opposing higher-timeframe premium array (for longs) that acts as the draw on liquidity.

sequence: Confirm that price is reacting from the weekly discount array behind the intended daily move.
Mark the new daily bullish fair value gap that defines the current directional leg.
Wait for price to trade back into that daily fair value gap.
Use the first reaction day: if the gap is respected, carry that bias into the following days.
Treat filled counter-trend daily fair value gaps as extra confirmation of the same draw on liquidity.

invalidation.text: The Daily FVG is 'disrespected' if a daily candle body closes entirely through it (e.g., closing below a bullish FVG).
The bias becomes low probability if price requires multiple deep retracements (stings) into the FVG over many days before expanding.

filters.text: Do not trade towards a lower timeframe FVG (like 5m or 1m) for daily bias context; use 4H, Daily, Weekly, Monthly.
Avoid trading neutral days. If the bias is unclear or price action is low probability, do not trade.

entry_rule.text: The entry model is separate from the bias read; once the daily bias is established, any compatible lower-timeframe execution model may be used.
entry_rule.quote: the entry model is completely irrelevant you can get very creative with your Edge model

target_rule.text: Target the opposing weekly premium/discount array or the next daily liquidity draw that sits beyond the respected daily FVG.
target_rule.quote: you target what the price action where we have no fair value gaps left

management.notes: Manage risk by moving to break even and taking profits.

presenter_claims.claim: Using this method has allowed him to outperform every hedge fund in the world.

strategies.notes: Context framework, not an entry model. The weekly framing is the presenter's premium/discount-array read, not the engine's structure bias. Filled counter-trend daily FVGs corroborate the active draw on liquidity but are not required as a separate step. The target text also mentions daily legs with no FVGs left; that alternative remains narrative-only.

uncertainties.issue: Low-probability weekly context behind the daily FVG is not encoded
uncertainties.why: The presenter says a daily FVG is weaker when an opposing weekly FVG sits 'right behind it', but he gives no exact distance or overlap rule for that weekly conflict.

uncertainties.issue: Multiple-day repeated stings before expansion are not quantified
uncertainties.why: The lesson says a strong daily FVG should react on the first day and that many deep revisits lower the probability, but it gives no exact candle-count or depth threshold.

confidence.reason: The presenter repeatedly and clearly explains the mechanics of reading FVGs for bias.

fvgs.presenter_calls_it: weak fair value gap / fully rebalanced
disrespected fair value gap / fully closing below
strong fair value gap / only wicking

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Presenter points out a daily fair value gap that is tapped four times and fully rebalanced, indicating it is weak.
Price disrespects another daily fair value gap by fully closing below it, which suggests a larger weekly fair value gap below is drawing price.
Price wicks into the weekly fair value gap, showing respect. Strong fair value gaps only need one sting before expanding.
A new strong daily fair value gap is formed and respected with a single wick, providing the daily bias for the subsequent days.

examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter emphasizes reading the 'story' of FVGs. Disrespected (closed through) FVGs and weak FVGs (multiple taps) tell you where price is NOT going, while respected (wicked) FVGs confirm the true directional bias.

may_differ.reason: Traidle calculates pure candle closes relative to the gap edges, while the presenter emphasizes the visual 'respect' via wicks on the specific timeframe.

uncertainties.why: I am working from a transcript without visual access to the chart. Cannot verify OHLC values or precise price levels.
